latin: Tenendo communem uiam theologorum, quod foelicitas sit in intellectu uel in uoluntate, dico duas conclusiones, quarum prima est haec: quod intellectus ad foelicitatem non perueniret nisi esset actus uoluntatis, qui in hoc est ipso actu intellectus potior.
translation: Holding to the theologians' common view that happiness resides in the intellect or in the will, I offer two conclusions; the first is that the intellect could not reach happiness without an act of will, which here outranks the act of intellect itself.
translation_note: Argued within the 'common way' framework Pico is not himself committed to (cf. 3>43, 4>4, 4>11); paired with 4>25 as its second conclusion.
